actions.body: Review everything on the last stage before you send. We come back within 3-5 business days with your business score, the all-in rate, the fixed amount you would repay each business day, and the backstop date — the day anything still outstanding falls due in full. Sending an application is not an approval, and nothing is owed until you sign.
actions.title: Sending, and what follows

documents.body: Nothing here is new paperwork. The charter and business registration are PDFs, and the e-invoice data must be the signed electronic original — XML files, or a ZIP of them. A PDF or a screenshot of an invoice is not accepted, because it can be edited and so proves nothing about your revenue.

stages.body: Your legal papers, then your e-invoices and tax filings — your revenue and costs are read from them — then your CIC report and a review screen. You can move back and forth freely; nothing is sent until you press send on the last stage.

lite.costsBasis: No filing says which costs are fixed and which move with sales, so one rule is applied. Fixed costs are your management expense (line 24 on a TT133 statement, line 26 on a TT200 one) plus your financial expense (line 22, interest included). Other variable costs are your selling expense (line 25); a TT133 statement has no such line, so for it this is 0.

error.top1_exceeds_top3: Your largest customer is one of the top three, so this cannot exceed the top-3 share.
error.worst_exceeds_best: The weakest month cannot be higher than the best month.

sme.step1How: Retrieve the official signed copy of your Company Charter and the Certificate of Business Registration.
sme.step1Why: To verify the company's internal regulations, ownership structure, and legal registration status.
sme.step2HowFilings: In HTKK, export your latest year-end financial statement package (XML) and the monthly VAT declarations for the last 24 months. Put them in one folder and upload it as a single .zip.
sme.step2HowInvoices: On the tax portal, export the invoice list for each of the last 12 months (one .xlsx per month), put the 12 files in one folder, and upload the folder as a single .zip.
sme.step2Why: To see how much your company sells and how steadily, month by month and against the year before, and what it costs you to earn that revenue. Trend and stability matter more to your rate than any single year's total, and the costs show how large a daily repayment your business can comfortably carry.
sme.step3How: Visit the State Bank of Vietnam CIC portal, log in with your business credentials, request a business credit report, and download it as PDF.
sme.step3Why: To see how your business has repaid past loans, from the State Bank's CIC records.

faqPage.ctaText: Our team is happy to walk you through the platform and how it fits your business or portfolio.

general.a1: FundLok connects SMEs in Vietnam with investors. Businesses raise funding and repay a fixed amount each business day; investors fund them and see the data behind each business.
general.a2: A bank loan usually has a fixed monthly instalment. FundLok uses a small fixed amount each business day, matched to a business that takes money in daily, and the term can stretch if verified revenue drops (with interest on the extra time).
general.a3: No. FundLok is not a bank or a lender. It is a technology platform that arranges funding between SMEs and investors, routes repayments and shows every transaction.
general.a4: Technology does the repetitive work: reading documents, checking them against tax records, preparing offers, routing funds and tracking every daily repayment. People review the decisions.
general.a5: Accounts support two-factor authentication and passkeys, connections are encrypted, and investor funds sit with custodial bank partners rather than with FundLok.
general.a6: No. Every application is reviewed, and funding and investing both carry risk. FundLok makes the process clearer, but it does not remove business or repayment risk. Whether a business gets funded is up to investors, and FundLok does not control that.
general.a7: Yes. FundLok arranges funding for SMEs in Vietnam. Investors provide the capital and the credit agreement is between the investor and the business. FundLok is not a bank, is not a lender, and does not lend its own money. A business declares a term of 1 to 6 months, repays a fixed amount each business day, and the total repayable is set at signing. If verified revenue drops, the term can stretch out and the daily repayment gets smaller. Interest applies to the extra time, so the total goes up.
general.q2: How is FundLok different from a traditional loan?
general.q4: How does FundLok use technology in its process?
general.q6: Does FundLok guarantee funding or returns?
general.q7: Does FundLok provide funding for SMEs in Vietnam?
general.title: General questions

investor.a1: Anyone who completes sign-up and identity verification can browse and fund listings. You can start from 10,000,000 VND.
investor.a2: Browse listings, review each business's score, verified revenue, fees and backstop date, then choose how much to put in.
investor.a3: Funds sit with our custodial bank partners. Money moves in only two directions: to a verified SME account under a signed agreement, or back to the investor who sent it. FundLok does not own these funds and cannot draw on them for its own purposes.
investor.a4: FundLok does not own investor funds and cannot draw on them: we hold instruction rights within conditions the custodial bank enforces. The credit agreement is between the investor and the SME; FundLok is not a party to it, and the investor bears the credit risk if a business underperforms.
investor.a5: Each business day's repayments are split across the investors in that facility, in proportion to what each put in, and show in your account. You can withdraw repaid funds to your verified bank account.
investor.a6: Funding progress, each business day's repayments, fees, and any warning or watchlist status on the businesses you fund.
investor.q4: How are investor funds held, and who bears the risk?
investor.q6: What can investors track on FundLok?
investor.title: For investors

msme.a1: SMEs in Vietnam that pass verification and whose revenue can support a daily repayment. Funding typically ranges from 20,000,000 to 100,000,000 VND.
msme.a2: Your business registration certificate, your VAT declarations and e-invoices (the signed electronic originals), your cost figures, and your CIC report.
msme.a3: We read your tax records and financial figures, compare them with sector data, and a reviewer checks the result.
msme.a4: Yes. You see the full offer, including the rate, the daily amount, the fees and the backstop date, before you confirm. Nothing is owed until you sign.
msme.a5: You repay a fixed amount each business day until the total is cleared. The total is set at signing. If verified revenue drops, the term can stretch out and the daily repayment gets smaller; interest on the extra time raises the total. There is no prepayment penalty, and you know the backstop date from the day you sign.
msme.a6: Because every business earns differently. A daily repayment suits businesses that take money in every day, and if verified revenue drops the term can stretch so the daily amount gets smaller.

specialPage.subtitle: Our vision, and how the model works for businesses and investors.
specialPage.title: Why FundLok

vision.description: When financing fits the business, SMEs grow more sustainably, investors gain greater confidence, and the economy functions more efficiently.
vision.highlight: And SME credit becomes something investors can assess on evidence
vision.paragraph1: Cash flow, growth pace, and repayment pressure are not the same for every business.
vision.paragraph2: That is why we build flexible capital solutions that adapt to each real-world situation.
vision.smeStory: FundLok believes every SME has a different story

whySpecial.fittingDesc: Tailored financing that aligns with the natural cycles of business growth.
whySpecial.fittingItem2: Loan size to fit, terms from 1 to 6 months
whySpecial.fittingItem3: Apply with documents you already have
whySpecial.safetyDesc: SME financing priced from a business score. The score is a reference that FundLok assesses itself, not a guarantee. Returns are targets, and the investor bears the credit risk.
whySpecial.safetyItem2: Every movement recorded with a reference
whySpecial.safetyItem3: If revenue drops, the term can stretch out so the daily repayment gets smaller
whySpecial.transparencyDesc: Decisions built on verified tax data, with each step recorded.
whySpecial.transparencyItem1: Document reading, loan assessment and interest calculation are automated
whySpecial.transparencyItem2: Data submitted must be from verified sources to protect all parties
whySpecial.transparencyItem3: Repayment status updated every business day

termsPage.noResults: No clauses found matching your search term.
termsPage.noticeBanner: FundLok is a technology and arranger platform operating within reviewed legal boundaries. Investor funds sit with custodial bank partners: FundLok does not own them, has no right to draw on them for its own purposes, and holds only instruction rights within conditions the bank enforces. FundLok is not a bank and does not lend its own money. The credit agreement is between the investor and the SME, and the investor bears the credit risk.
termsPage.noticeTitle: How FundLok operates and where funds are held

items.2: One missed payment raises a flag, for closer loan monitoring.
items.3: Reinvest sooner to put compounding to work.

dailyBenefit.title: Money comes back from day one.

disclosure.body: Every listing shows what's behind it before you commit.
disclosure.title: Fund real businesses.

journey.body: Pick, commit, fund, then get paid every business day. Funds sit with our custodial bank partners.
journey.title: From listing to repayment.

riskRate.body: Stronger businesses pay less; riskier ones pay more.
riskRate.title: Risk sets the rate.

assessment.body: Your reference score comes from tax records and e-invoices, not assets.
assessment.title: We look at how you run your business.

daily.body: Your monthly total is exactly what you'd pay monthly. You don't pay a single đồng more; each payment is just lighter.
daily.title: Same money, just split by day.

extension.body: Relief becomes extra time. Your daily amount drops; the total rises slightly from interest on the added days.
extension.title: Pay less each day, for a bit longer.

intro.body: No property to pledge. Repayment fits how your business earns.
intro.title: Capital that follows your revenue.

relief.body: After the month closes, send us your verified revenue. If your agreed share of it is less than you paid, the difference becomes relief.
relief.title: Slow month? Request relief.

items.1: Within a month, every day is paid in full.
items.2: Paying less without approval counts as a missed payment, so contact FundLok and we'll help.
items.3: Anything left falls due on the final settlement date.
